title: Residual growth on the GLOBAL head at full-data scale: growth-dictionary prefixes vs blind-greedy selection, appended to the base SPM+sqrt head and re-fused, at the M155-registered budgets {256, 2048}
registered_in: analysis/RESEARCH_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_v23.md section 4 M156 / section 6 execution log (16 Aug 2026)
question: Does residual-targeted growth on the global head's error rows pay at the M155-permitted budgets {256, 2048}, beyond what blind-greedy selection of the same pool explains?

artifacts.note: all under the M141 cell-2 row schedule (409,832 train rows), the same order as spm1923_fulltrain

base.note: the promoted SPM+sqrt full-data head (C4 p=0.5, penalty 0.1); its test read is the a1 anchor AND the static arm of the gate

sparse.note: used only to rebuild the whitener for the a2/a4 anchors (M145 protocol); the arms themselves read the cached f6144 codes

growth.budgets_note: the M155-registered rungs {256, 2048}; 2048 is the largest clearing power of two (ceil(76670/(4*2048)) = 10 >= floor 10)
growth.dictionary_note: first g atoms of the cached f6144 pool = the [11,100]-permuted shared pool's first 6144 atoms; atom a owns columns {a, 6144+a, 12288+a, 18432+a} (the M103 interleaved bin-major layout). No new encode: the arm codes are column-extracted from the cached memmaps.
growth.head_fit_note: growth and control heads are fitted on the SAME rows (the base head's train error rows) with the same ridge penalty 1.0; the arms differ ONLY in how the dictionary is chosen.

control.mechanism: M108 arm (c) blind greedy (group-OMP vs centred one-hot, select_discriminative) over the error-row features, pool 6144 atoms, budget 2048, GPU port (_select_discriminative_gpu) with the M145 order-parity check; on parity failure the control arm is VOID (section 6 amendment) and only growth-vs-static is adjudicated

anchors.a1_note: the promoted head's full-data test read (the M155 anchor), tol 1e-9
anchors.a2_note: the M145 specialist-path anchor: d0 512-atom own-domain accuracy from the rebuilt whitener + d0 candidates, [11,100] prefix, ridge 1.0
anchors.a4_note: cached-code reproduction: a fresh GPU encode of the first 64 train rows with the rebuilt 6144-atom dictionary reproduces the cached f6144 codes

premise.note: n_error > 0 hard-fails; the full run requires n_error == 76670 exactly (the M155 sealed population) else VOID; per-budget floor ceil(n_error/(4g)) >= 10 else the budget is void, not negative

phase2.note: the M143b train protocol: fit 80% / select penalty on 20% of the train rows, refit on all train rows, evaluate on the test rows

gate.registered: per budget g: growth_fused >= static + 0.005 AND growth_fused > control_fused, where static = the base head's test read; control >= growth at any budget means the gain is not residual targeting's and that budget's growth claim fails; a void control arm leaves growth-vs-control non-adjudicable and the budget cannot pass
gate.consequence_passed: residual-targeted growth lifts the global-head system beyond the base read, and blind greedy selection cannot reproduce the lift: the growth mechanism is the targeting, not the dictionary draw.
gate.consequence_fired: growth does not clear the registered margin over the base read, or the blind-greedy control reaches it: M156 closes as a scoped negative on this corpus and the base head stands.

ops_ledger.note: both arms report the g-atom encode-equivalent MACs over train+test rows (disclosed, not matched away); the control additionally its error-row pool encode + OMP selection MACs; growth-vs-control is the matched-cost comparison.
